items.title: Robotics startup SynapX reportedly raises hundreds of millions of yuan, with Midea joining
items.summary: Chinese robotics startup SynapX has secured several hundred million yuan in new funding, with Midea among the new investors, Blue Whale News reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The financing follows a $50 million round in June; the full investor list and exact amount were not disclosed.

items.title: Lenovo’s Lecoo launches walking-assist exoskeleton from RMB 6,999
items.summary: Lenovo’s Lecoo brand has listed the Xingzhe ONE wearable exoskeleton in China, with an introductory price of RMB 6,999 and sales scheduled to begin on November 28. The device weighs 1.8 kilograms and uses powered hip joints to assist walking and other outdoor activities.

items.title: Honor launches 700 series with rear displays and 9,000mAh batteries
items.summary: Honor launched its 700 smartphone series in China on Monday, adding rear displays and 9,000mAh batteries across a lineup starting at RMB 3,399 before subsidies. The 700S, 700 and 700 Pro are available for preorder, with sales scheduled to begin on November 27.

items.title: ByteDance opens invitation-only beta for Xiaodou personal AI assistant
items.summary: ByteDance’s Doubao team opened a public beta for its personal AI assistant Xiaodou on Tuesday, giving invited users access to a separate product whose capabilities will gradually be introduced into the main Doubao app. The beta requires an invitation code and includes an allocation of free usage credits.

items.title: Nothing previews Ear (note) AI earbuds that record calls and meetings
items.summary: Nothing plans to launch Ear (note), a pair of earbuds with AI recording and transcription features, on December 8. Co-founder and CEO Carl Pei demonstrated the product to Bloomberg, showing how microphones in the earbuds and charging case can capture phone calls and in-person conversations.

items.summary: Chinese question-and-answer platform Zhihu has disclosed an indirect investment in DeepSeek through a private equity fund. items.title: New York cracks down on subscription fees for built-in car features
items.summary: Heated seats and hands-free driving are among the features caught up in New York's push to stop drivers paying again for equipment their cars already have.

items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source tool that puts temporary protections on running Linux systems while their owners work on a patch. items.title: GPT-6.2 Comes to Standard ChatGPT; Internal Evaluations Show Better Image Understanding and Instruction Following, Excluding Free and Go
items.summary: OpenAI is gradually rolling out GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday conversation to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise. It outperformed GPT-6 in OpenAI's internal evaluations of image understanding, complex requests, and web search.

items.title: From bakery worker to tech tycoon: How Malaysia's Tan Eng Kee built a global factory automation empire
items.summary: Born into a poor family in Penang, Tan Eng Kee worked at a bakery as a teenager to help support his family before co-founding factory automation company Greatech Technology and becoming a billionaire.

items.title: Hila Klein Exits ‘H3 Podcast’ Following Ethan Klein Affair: ‘I’m Devastated That Things Have Come to This’
items.summary: Hila Klein is officially exiting the “H3 Podcast” a month after it was revealed that her co-host and husband, Ethan Klein, had been having a six-month affair. The news follows Hila’s October announcement that the show would be on an “indefinite hiatus” amid the scandal’s fallout.

items.title: How IT can delegate password management without losing control
items.summary: IT is expected to secure company accounts, but it doesn’t always control how they’re created or shared. Departments manage their own tools and grant access to colleagues or contractors, often without involving IT. This leaves IT responsible for accounts it may not even know about.

items.summary: Agent swarms are really distributed systems problems in disguise.

items.title: FCC to Reconsider U.S. Market Access for Foreign-Licensed Satellites, Proposes Reflecting Home-Country Restrictions
items.summary: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission proposes imposing in the United States restrictions similar to those U.S. satellite operators face abroad. A vote is planned for December; satellites licensed in Japan have previously received U.S. market access.

items.title: Jensen Huang is ‘too big to fire,’ putting Nvidia’s governance in focus: analysts
items.summary: Jensen Huang’s return has underscored Nvidia’s deep reliance on its founder, putting the company's board oversight and corporate governance under scrutiny.

items.title: Eruption Extends Iwo Jima’s Beach
items.summary: A volcanic eruption just off the southeast shore of the Pacific island has reshaped the coast, but it’s unclear how long the new land will survive.

items.title: Stalwart: Open-source Microsoft Exchange replacement
items.summary: Stalwart, an open source mail server, shipped version 1.2.0 with support for the protocols Exchange clients speak: MAPI over HTTP, Exchange Web Services (EWS), Exchange ActiveSync and Autodiscover.

items.title: Australia Agrees to Penalties of Up to 5% of Global Revenue and a Direct Right of Action in Digital Duty of Care Bill
items.summary: Australia's Labor government and the Greens have agreed on amendments to the Digital Duty of Care bill. Alongside penalties of up to 5% of global revenue, they agreed to give Australians harmed online a direct right to sue social media providers.

items.title: Chrome Fixes Critical CVE-2026-134401, Which Could Allow Arbitrary Code Execution Outside the Sandbox
items.summary: Google has released a Chrome security update. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency assigned a CVSS base score of 9.6, and fixes are available for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and the Extended Stable channel used by organizations.

items.title: Samsung Odyssey G6 (G60H) Launches in the U.S. in December, Reaching 1,100Hz at HD and 600Hz at WQHD
items.summary: Samsung plans to sell the 27-inch Odyssey G6 (G60H) gaming monitor in the U.S. starting in December 2026. It supports up to 600Hz at WQHD and 1,100Hz at HD, letting players choose detail or refresh frequency for each game.

items.title: datasette-charts 0.2a0
items.summary: Release: datasette-charts 0.2a0 I introduced this new charting plugin for Datasette yesterday . Today it's gained integration with Datasette Agent , so now you can ask chat for a chart and it will create one for you using the same underlying chart suggestion and generation tools.

items.title: Manjaro 27.0 Stable Update Ends KDE Plasma X11 Sessions; Switch to Wayland or a TTY Before Updating
items.summary: The Manjaro 27.0 stable update has begun, bringing KDE Plasma 6.8.2 and GNOME 51.1. Plasma users in an X11 session are instructed to switch to Wayland or a TTY before updating.

items.title: CrowdStrike Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Zscaler; Monitoring Data Will Also Train Security AI
items.summary: CrowdStrike has signed an agreement to acquire Zscaler. After the acquisition, it plans to combine endpoint protection with network access control and use both companies' telemetry for threat detection and training security AI models.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.331 Reportedly Loses Tool-Definition References After Conversation Compaction
items.summary: After Claude Code compacts conversation history, reports say it may search again for loaded tools or call them without access to their definitions. Official Claude Agent SDK documentation anticipates renewed searches after compaction, while production cases also show input-validation failures.

items.title: A new APNIC Academy experience is coming on 30 November 2026
items.summary: On 30 November 2026, APNIC Academy 3.0 will launch with an improved learning experience shaped by learner feedback, making it easier to find training, access resources, and develop skills in core Internet technologies.

items.title: Amazon to Acquire Decart's AI Optimization Technology, Aiming to Strengthen Trainium Through Software
items.summary: Amazon has signed an agreement to acquire Decart technology that makes AI training and inference more efficient and to hire its development team. The technology also supports NVIDIA GPUs and Google TPUs; Amazon aims to improve its Trainium AI chips and reduce compute costs.
